name: The Tracker Toolkit
oneLiner: One typed Azure DevOps client every agent shares — reads and writes work items live, or against local fixtures with zero credentials.
lead: A single `AdoClient` that reads and writes ADO work items — stories, bugs, test points, test runs — for every agent in the toolkit. It replaces ~85 scripts that each re-implemented the same base64 auth header and hard-coded one org/project/board. Org, project, and PAT now come from config; drop the PAT and the identical client transparently backs onto a `fixtures/ado` FixtureStore, so the same code path runs in CI with no network and no secrets.
chore: The prior setup had ~85 scripts, each re-implementing the same `Basic base64(':' + PAT)` auth and each with the org, project, and board URL baked in. Rotating a PAT or switching boards meant hand-editing dozens of files. And none of them ran without a live board and a valid PAT — no offline demo, no unit-testable path.
instead: One client. Auth is defined once; `apiBase`, `project`, and `testPlanId` come from `loadConfig().ado`, so nothing is tied to a specific tenant. When no PAT is present the constructor flips `offline: true` and routes every call through a `FixtureStore` over `fixtures/ado/{id}.json` — same methods, same return types, no network. Live and offline are chosen automatically by whether a PAT exists.
whyItMatters: One typed, config-driven client replaces ~85 fragile single-purpose scripts. Point it at any tenant via env vars, or at fixtures for a credential-free demo — the calling code is identical either way, so the same agents run in CI and in production.

howItWorks.step: The constructor builds the auth header once from config and, if no PAT is present, switches itself into fixture-backed offline mode instead of failing.
howItWorks.explain: Auth is `Basic base64(':' + PAT)` — the PAT goes in the **password** half of HTTP Basic with an empty username, which is why the string is `:${pat}`; this one line replaces the header ~85 scripts each rebuilt. `patWrite` is preferred over `pat` so write-scoped calls get the stronger token when one exists. `this.offline` was already decided by `loadConfig()` as `!pat`, so **no PAT means no live store** — the constructor builds a `FixtureStore` over `fixtures/ado` instead, and `persist ?? false` keeps it read-only by default so a demo never mutates committed fixtures.

howItWorks.step: Raw ADO field dictionaries (`System.Title`, `System.AssignedTo`, ...) are mapped to one flat, typed `WorkItem` shape before anything downstream sees them.
howItWorks.explain: The **single choke-point** where a raw ADO `fields` bag becomes a flat typed `WorkItem`, and both the live REST path and the fixture path call it — so nothing downstream ever touches a `System.Title`-style key or parses a relation URL. Field keys are indirected through the `F.*` constants (`F.tags`, `F.assignedTo`, …), so a schema rename is one edit, not a grep. Note the defensive fallbacks: absent `fields` becomes `{}`, a missing type becomes `'Unknown'`, and `tags` is split on `;` **only when non-empty** so an empty tag string yields `[]` rather than `['']`. Each relation is remapped to carry a `targetId` already pulled from its URL via `targetIdFromUrl`.

howItWorks.step: `getWorkItem` branches on the store: fixtures resolve `{id}.json` locally, live hits `GET /wit/workitems/{id}?$expand=relations` — same normalized return either way.
howItWorks.explain: One method, one `WorkItem` return type, two sources chosen solely by whether `this.store` is set (offline) or null (live) — the caller genuinely cannot tell them apart. Offline, a fixture miss is a **hard throw** (`[ado:offline] work item {id} not found in fixtures`) rather than a silent null, so a demo referencing a non-existent id fails loudly instead of returning garbage. Live, `$expand=relations` is requested so the normalized item carries its parent/child links, matching what the fixture path already stores. Both branches funnel through the same `normalize()`, guaranteeing an identical shape.

howItWorks.step: `createWorkItem` builds the JSON-Patch document once via `patchesFor()`, then either writes a fixture file or `POST`s to `/wit/workitems/${type}`.
howItWorks.explain: The JSON-Patch document is built **once** by `patchesFor()` and then either replayed into a synthetic fixture or POSTed to ADO, so the write logic isn't duplicated per branch. Offline, `store.nextId()` mints an id, an empty `RawWorkItem` is stamped with the type and the same patches via `applyPatchesToRaw`, then persisted — the patch list is thus the single source of truth for both paths. Live, note the `$$` in the URL: one `$` is ADO's literal work-item-type prefix (`/wit/workitems/$Bug`) and the second escapes it inside the template string, and the trailing `true` flags this as a `json-patch` write. Either way the result comes back through `normalize()`.

howItWorks.step: `getTestPoints` returns a test suite's runnable test points — from the live test-plan API, or synthesized one-per-fixture-Test-Case offline — so a run can be posted against them.
howItWorks.explain: A test *point* is the runnable pairing of a Test Case with a suite — you post outcomes against points, not cases — so this method must produce them either way. Offline there is no plan/suite structure, so it **synthesizes** one point per Test Case fixture with a deterministic `id = 900000 + testCaseId`; the large offset keeps synthetic point ids from colliding with real work-item ids. Live, it queries `/testplan/plans/{planId}/suites/{suiteId}/testpoint` (falling back to `this.cfg.testPlanId` when no `planId` is passed) and maps each result's `testCaseReference?.id` down to `0` if absent. Both yield the same `TestPoint[]` a run can be stamped against.

howItWorks.step: `fileOne` turns a `TestFailure` into a filed, parent-linked bug — with `dedupe` to reuse an open match and `dryRun` to preview without writing.
howItWorks.explain: The bug-filing path, with two short-circuits before any write. `dedupe` first calls `findOpenBug(title, bugType)` and, on a hit, returns `action: 'reused'` with the existing id — so re-running the same failing suite doesn't spawn duplicate bugs. `dryRun` returns `action: 'would-create'` with a null `bugId`, letting a caller preview exactly what would be filed without touching the board. Only past both does it build the `[Test Failure] {test} ({environment})` title and `reproHtml(failure)` description, then create the bug via `createWorkItem`, wiring `failure.parentId` into a `DEFAULTS.parentRel` relation so the bug hangs under its story — and the three `action` values (`reused`/`would-create`/`created`) keep the outcome auditable.

examples.caption: File a bug from a test failure, offline (no PAT)
examples.input: A `TestFailure` for `checkout.spec: TC-014` (timeout), run with `offline: true`.
examples.output: A bug is written to the fixture store — title `[Test Failure] checkout.spec: TC-014`, severity, error text, and a parent relation — proving the full file path works before any PAT is set.

examples.caption: Retarget to another tenant
examples.input: `ADO_ORG` / `ADO_PROJECT` / `ADO_PAT` set to a different org's board.
examples.output: The same client reads and writes that board's live work items — no code change, `offline` flips to `false` the moment a PAT is present.

examples.caption: Post a batch of test outcomes
examples.input: A list of test cases with pass/fail results for a plan/suite.
examples.output: A test run is opened, each point is stamped Passed or Failed, and the run is completed — same calls whether against the live plan or the offline fixture store.

underHood.heading: Loads config
underHood.whenRuns: In the constructor, once per client.
underHood.output: One `AdoConfig`, with `offline` set true automatically whenever no PAT is present.

underHood.heading: Live REST path
underHood.input: A work-item id, a WIQL query, or a `NewWorkItem`.
underHood.output: Normalized `WorkItem`s from the Azure DevOps REST API (api-version 7.0), auth header attached automatically.

underHood.heading: Fixture path
underHood.whenRuns: When no PAT is present — no code change.
underHood.input: The identical method calls a live run would make.
underHood.output: The same typed shapes, read from / written to `fixtures/ado/{id}.json` via `FixtureStore` — no network or secret.

underHood.heading: Failure to bug
underHood.output: A created bug, a reused open one (`dedupe`), or a `would-create` preview (`dryRun`), parent-linked.

underHood.heading: Post a run's outcomes
underHood.whenRuns: When a batch of results lands on a plan.
underHood.output: A completed test run — live on the real plan or in the fixture store — readable back for reporting.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Node.js (installed in step 1 below) — nothing else.
No credentials, board, database, or API key are needed for the demo below — that is the point of this module. A `.env` only matters later, if you point it at something real.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The toolkit is TypeScript on Node. One install per machine; no other runtime required.
steps.firstRun: First time on a new machine only.

steps.label: Clone and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the toolkit's only dependency (`dotenv`) into `node_modules`. No DB driver, no cloud SDK, no auth library — which is why the demos run credential-free.
steps.firstRun: Downloads everything (seconds — the dependency list is tiny).
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency list changed.

steps.label: (Optional) copy the env template — only to go live later.
steps.cmd:
cp .env.example .env
# then open .env and fill in ONLY the section you need
steps.why: Skippable for the demo — every capability is off by default and the demo runs on fixtures regardless. `.env` matters only once you point the toolkit at a real board, service, or database.

steps.label: Run the capability check.
steps.why: Prints a one-line scorecard per capability (tracker, API, database, AI) — on/off with a reason. With an empty `.env` everything reads `(off)`, which is expected: the demo needs none of them on.

steps.label: Run the tracker demo — query a story, file a bug, post outcomes.
steps.why: Exercises the real `AdoClient` end to end against `fixtures/ado` (`offline: true`, no PAT): queries a User Story via WIQL, files a bug from a synthetic `TestFailure`, and derives + posts Test Case outcomes — the same code path a live board takes.
steps.firstRun: Reads the fixture story, files an in-memory bug (`persist: false`, so committed fixtures are never modified), and prints the derived Test Case outcomes.
steps.rerun: Deterministic — fixtures never change, so a second run prints the identical story, bug fields, and Passed/Failed outcomes.

steps.label: Read the terminal output.
steps.cmd:
# nothing to open — this demo prints straight to the terminal:
#   1. Query a User Story (WIQL)
#   2. File a Bug from a test failure
#   3. Derive Test Case outcomes and post a run
#   4. Summary
steps.why: No file output; the log is the evidence — the story found (#101), the bug filed (#204, in-memory only), and the 3 derived Test Case outcomes (2 Passed, 1 Failed).

inputs.name: nothing
inputs.desc: Runs on the committed `fixtures/ado/*.json` — sample story, child tickets, and test cases. No board, PAT, or network.

inputs.name: ADO_ORG / ADO_PROJECT / ADO_PAT (optional)
inputs.desc: Set all three in `.env` to point the same client at a real Azure DevOps board; `offline` flips to `false` automatically once a PAT is present.

outputs.name: console log
outputs.desc: The story found, the bug filed (id, title, severity, links), and each Test Case's derived outcome (Passed/Failed) with its reason — all printed, nothing written to disk.

outputs.name: in-memory bug #204
outputs.desc: Created for the demo only (`persist: false`); `fixtures/ado` is never touched, so the demo is safe to rerun indefinitely.

runbook.rerun: Idempotent: the demo runs with `persist: false`, so nothing it creates is written back to the fixtures — rerun freely and get the identical story, bug, and outcomes. Point the same client at a live board (set `ADO_PAT`) and reruns instead reflect the board's current state.
runbook.integrate: Import directly: `import { AdoClient } from './src/core/ado'`, then `new AdoClient({ config: loadConfig().ado })` — with a PAT it hits the live board, without one it falls back to fixtures, so the same calling code runs in CI (offline) and production (live). Compose with `BugFilerAgent` (`agents/ado/bug-filer-agent`) and `TestResultsAgent` (`agents/ado/test-results-agent`) exactly as `examples/ado/demo.ts` does.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: run the tracker demo through a full query → file → post cycle against fixtures, zero credentials.
script: Open a terminal in the qa-agent-toolkit folder.
Say: 'This is the toolkit's board connector. Watch it run a full query-file-post cycle with zero credentials.'
Run `node -v` and `npm install`; say one line about the dependency list being tiny — no Azure SDK, no login library.
Run `npm run doctor`; point out ADO reads `(off)` — no ADO_ORG/PAT set — and say that's fine, it's not needed yet.
Run `npm run demo:ado`; narrate as the log prints: 'mode: OFFLINE (fixtures)'.
Point at the first block: story #101, 'As a user, I can reset my password...', 5 relations.
Point at the second block: Bug #204 filed with severity '1 - Critical', linked to the parent + test case.
Point at the third block: 3 Test Case outcomes — TC #201 Passed, TC #202 Failed (open bug #103), TC #203 Passed.
Read the closing line out loud: 'Zero Azure calls, zero secrets — same code path runs live with a PAT.'
Re-run the same command; show the output is byte-for-byte identical — the fixtures never changed.
Close: 'Fill in ADO_ORG, ADO_PROJECT and ADO_PAT in .env, and this exact command talks to your real board instead.'
